defects.mechanism: Registry.accept keyed operations only by operation_id. INV-301 (shop/north/op-41) and INV-302 (shop/south/op-41) have identical order/sku/action/qty but are distinct operations; the bare key falsely classified INV-302 as replay. Identity must be (tenant, warehouse, operation_id), with immutable payload (order_id, sku, action, qty). INV-303 is the actual north replay and must remain suppressed. The one-line identity correction preserves payload-conflict and stock/hold validation. ARC-CACHE-29 describes restart eviction in the retired r29 single-warehouse reservation cache, whereas config/routes.json selects r31 scoped-batch-v2 and src.pipeline.replay invokes the current projector without that cache. ARC-LOG-29 and ARC-SNAPSHOT-29 also describe the retired r29 route and cannot override current events.
defects.impact: OBS-INV-31/TRACE-INV-31 record accepted 1, replayed 2 and only 2 reserved units instead of accepted 2, replayed 1 and 4 reserved units. The south hold is missing, so the two-warehouse requirements in ORD-301 cannot be fulfilled. This contributes to the combined readiness failure in OBS-JOIN-31; checkout independently hides readiness as well.

defects.mechanism: select compared delivered_at rather than source revision. ORD-310 is revision 10/paid delivered at 09:00 UTC, while ORD-311 is revision 2/pending delivered at 09:05 UTC. The later delivery incorrectly replaces the newer snapshot. ORD-301/ORD-302 reproduce the same ordering across the combined checkpoint and suffix. Select the greatest numeric revision per (tenant, order_id), regardless of delivery time or input order, while retaining immutable status/capture/lines conflict detection for every duplicate revision. Newer pending snapshots remain valid; no terminal-status rule is added. ARC-POLL-29 recommends poll timestamps only because the retired r29 polling feed lacked source revisions. Current source-snapshot-v3 records contain revisions, so that advice is inapplicable. ARC-LOG-29 and ARC-SNAPSHOT-29 concern r29, not this feed.
defects.impact: OBS-ORD-31/TRACE-ORD-31 expose revision 2/pending/ready false instead of revision 10/paid/ready true even with sufficient inventory in the isolated checkout case. In the combined replay, the wrong pending status rejects all three refund deliveries as order_not_refundable, yielding zero refunded and net 1000, and masks the independent refund-identity defect. Correct checkout selection restores refund eligibility; the inventory correction also restores combined fulfillment readiness.

defects.mechanism: Ledger.accept used (tenant, provider, attempt_id) as identity. REF-321 and REF-322 deliver the same shop/atlas/R-17 refund for O-17, amount 400, with attempts delivery-a and delivery-b; different delivery attempts must not create new logical refunds. Identity must be (tenant, provider, refund_id), with immutable payload (order_id, amount_minor). Registration remains before eligibility and capture checks so previously rejected refunds also replay once without reconsideration; retries never consume budget. REF-323 is distinct refund R-18 for 500. ARC-MONEY-29 concerns rounding in retired r29 decimal-file imports; r31 settled-deliveries-v2 uses integer minor amounts, including 400/400/500 here, so rounding does not cause this incident. ARC-LOG-29 and ARC-SNAPSHOT-29 refer to the retired r29 route.
defects.impact: With the valid paid ORD-320 snapshot, the broken ledger counts both R-17 deliveries, spends 800 of captured 1000 and incorrectly rejects REF-323 as exceeds_capture. OBS-REF-31/TRACE-REF-31 record total 800, replayed 0 and that rejection. Correct accounting accepts R-17 once and R-18 once: total 900, replayed 1 and no rejection. Once inventory and checkout are also corrected, combined output has ready_orders 1, reserved_units 4, refunded_minor 900, rejected_refunds 0 and net_minor 100.
